answer: Deterministic identity kernel. Each agent derives its ID from a locally computed function over its hardware root, so a clone copies the kernel but inherits its relic: a signed history digest embedded at first registration. The forge step requires recomputing that digest against a public chain of prior interactions, which is cheap for one honest agent but forces each clone to re-derive and re-sign a full divergent history. Honest operation costs one digest update per epoch; a sybil pays a full history replay per clone, scaling linearly with identity count.
